scope.purpose: Show a quantity (unread messages, items, selected rows) as a compact pill next to the thing it counts.
useCases: Standalone next to a tab label, a navigation item or a list header, with an accessible label giving the number its meaning (8 unread messages).
Inside the Button trailing slot, as text-like content placed by its box that inherits the button's content color and takes the button's size.
Large quantities capped at a maximum and shown as an overflow (99+ by default, max configurable).
Zero shown as 0 when the integration chooses to render the counter (0 selected rows); hiding an empty quantity is the integration's choice.
exclusions: Status or category words (Badge, wave 1, planned).
Free text, units or formatted amounts (plain text, DataField).
A dot indicator without a number (Badge or a later indicator).
Live announcements when the value changes: the integration owns live regions.
A colored or filled emphasis axis (neutral, accent, danger): waits for an indicator color family shared with Badge (open decision 2).
alternatives: Badge (planned) for a status or a category rather than a quantity.
Plain text when the number is part of a sentence or a data cell.
NumberInput (later) when the user edits the quantity.

fixtures: The Button review fixture examples/button/Fixtures.svelte (kind counter) is the current stand-in inside Button: inline-grid pill, min-inline-size 1.5em, padding-inline 0.4em, radius full, inset 1 px ring in currentColor, font-size 0.85em, tabular figures. Button examples and tests switch to the component once Counter passes its implementation gate.

decisionsTaken: value is a number (default 0, min 0), not a required string: the component owns the overflow rule (value > max shows max+), which needs a number, and a quantity is what the component means; free text belongs to Badge or plain text. The schema requires a default for numbers, so an omitted value shows 0 rather than failing.

max is a number (default 99, min 1); overflow shows max followed by a plus sign (99+). The accessible text is the visible text (99+), not the exact value: visible and announced text agree, which is what sighted screen reader users expect, and the pill stays compact. Exposed as the derived boolean state overflow.

label is an optional string: the accessible text is the visible number followed by label when set (8 unread messages). It is optional because inside a host (Button) the host decides whether the counter is announced at all, and next to a visible label (Inbox 8) the reading order already gives the meaning. The component guarantees that its text is readable and that label, when given, is part of it; the integration guarantees that a lone number has a meaning.

No showZero option: the counter always shows its value, 0 included; the integration knows whether 0 is meaningful (0 selected rows) or should disappear (0 unread), and conditional rendering is trivial on every platform.

No emphasis, intent or appearance axis in v1: the existing inventory offers action colors (for actions), status colors (Badge's territory) and selection colors, none of which is honest for a notification counter; and inside a Button the counter must inherit the button's content anyway. The single treatment is the one the user validated in the Button implementation review: border and digits in the inherited content color, no fill. A future filled or colored emphasis is recorded as open decision 2, to share with Badge.

No color role at all: the border and the value use the inherited content color (currentColor) in every context (standalone next to text, inside a solid, outline or ghost Button in any state). This is the only context-independent choice and it needs no contrast evidence of its own.

size is sm | md | lg with the Button's names (default md), so that an integration passes the host's size through without a mapping; the counter's typography is one step below the host's label at each size (fixture ratio 0.85: 10.2, 11.9, 13.6 px rounded to the 11, 12, 14 px primitives).

The container block size is the line box of the typography (no block padding) and the minimum inline size equals the block size, so a single digit is a circle; the counter has no control height and no interaction target because it is not interactive. The alternative, binding the block size to size.icon.{size} (16, 20, 24 px, equal to the Button slot's minimum block size), was considered and set aside because the brief and the validated fixture size the counter by its typography; it is mentioned at the gate.

paddingInline binds space.content.xs (compact 2, standard 4, comfortable 6 px): the content spacing family is the one for spacing inside content, the standard value matches the validated fixture (0.4em of 11.9 px = 4.8 px) and a density-dependent padding follows the Button's own spacing, which also shrinks with density. space.content.sm (4, 8, 12) was too wide at standard.
borderWidth binds border.width.default (1 px) and radius binds radius.full, as in the fixture; the border is drawn inside the container edge so the box the host places is the visible pill.
Digits are tabular (fixture, and the numeral typography family already carries tnum), so counters of the same size and digit count have the same width in lists and tabs.

Typography role left unbound on purpose: no existing role is honest (numeral.sm/md/lg are 14/16/24 px, too big for a counter that must sit below a 12 to 16 px label; caption.sm/md are 400 weight without tabular figures and have no lg step; label.sm/md/lg are the host's own sizes). Binding typography.numeral.{size} would validate but render a 24 px counter in a lg Button. The proposed roles are in open decision 1; the contract binds the role typography once the reviewer picks the family.

Parts limited to container and value; the accessible label is not a visual part. No events, no interaction states: the counter never reacts to its host's hover, pressed, loading or disabled states beyond inheriting the content color (Button fades its trailing content while loading and gives it the disabled content color).
Forced-colors rule kept in the contract (decision register: every component with a border handles forced colors): the border stays visible in the system text color.
The roadmap progress row, the token files and the token inventory were not touched in this worktree (orchestrator instruction: shared files are edited by the orchestrator at the grouped gate).

Implementation (2026-10-14): the root element is the container part (class ggb-counter, no ggb-counter__container layer); Button has a separate root only because it is an interaction target. The hidden accessible label uses the helper class ggb-counter__label, not a contract part, following Button's ggb-button__name precedent.

Implementation (2026-10-14): a non-finite value (NaN, Infinity, null from an empty number field) shows 0 and a non-finite max falls back to 99; max is floored and kept at least 1 so the overflow text is itself a counter value. The accessible text is the visible text (99+), as decided at the contract gate.

Implementation (2026-10-14): the accessible label is a visually hidden span that starts with a space, kept by white-space: pre, rather than aria-label (which would replace the visible text) or a space-less span (Chromium's accessibility tree concatenates inline text without inserting one). Verified through the Chromium accessibility tree (CDP) rather than Playwright's accessible-name computation, which does not name a generic span.

Implementation (2026-10-14): flex: none on the root. An explicit min-inline-size replaces a flex item's automatic content floor, so the first draft let a narrow flex parent shrink the box and the digits spilled past the border; with flex: none the counter overflows its parent instead, as the contract requires (never wrapped or truncated).

Implementation (2026-10-14): in forced-colors mode the outline color is currentColor, not CanvasText, so the border follows the forced text color of the host (ButtonText in a Button, GrayText in a disabled Button); verified in Chromium 141.

Implementation (2026-10-14): min-inline-size uses the lh unit (no generated lineHeight helper exists and adding one would change shared tooling); Chromium resolves it in 1/64 px layout units, equal to the laid-out block size, so the browser test compares the minimum with the element's height at 0.005 px and with the token line box at 0.05 px.

Implementation (2026-10-14): the geometry test asserts width = max(line box, digit + 2 x padding) rather than 'a single digit is square', which the first draft assumed and which is false at comfortable density (padding 6 px per side); the square is still asserted wherever the padding allows it. The code was right; the assertion is the contract's rule.

implementationNotes: Svelte: <span class="ggb-counter" data-size data-overflow?> is the root and the container part (no separate target layer: not interactive); <span class="ggb-counter__value"> holds the digits; when label is set a visually hidden <span class="ggb-counter__label"> follows, starting with a space (white-space: pre keeps it) so the accessible text is one phrase (8 unread messages); no role, aria-label or tabindex. Native attributes pass through, class is merged, ref is bindable. No Bits UI primitive: there are no native semantics to borrow.

Formatting: value -> Number.isFinite ? max(0, floor) : 0; max -> finite ? max(1, floor) : 99; overflow = value > max; text = Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 0 }) of value, or of max followed by U+002B. The locale is the runtime's (server or browser); grouping only shows once max is raised above 999.

CSS: display inline-grid; place-items center; font from --ggb-counter-typography with the letterSpacing and fontFeatureSettings helpers (tnum) plus font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; padding-inline var(--ggb-counter-paddingInline); padding-block 0, or calc((1lh - 1cap) / 2) with text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic on the value where supported (@supports), so the digits are centered on their cap height in an unchanged line box; min-inline-size: 1lh (Chromium resolves it in 1/64 px layout units: 15.3906 px for sm, equal to the laid-out block size); flex: none so a flex parent cannot shrink the box below its content; white-space nowrap; border-radius var(--ggb-counter-radius); background: rgb(from currentColor r g b / var(--ggb-counter-surfaceOpacity)); border 0; a transparent inset outline of borderWidth is always present and becomes the edge in forced-colors mode (outline-color: currentColor, which follows the forced text color: CanvasText standalone, ButtonText in a Button, GrayText when the Button is disabled).

Measured geometry (base, Inter): block size 15.4 / 16.8 / 19.6 px for sm / md / lg in every density; one digit is a square at compact and standard; at comfortable the padding (6 px per side) plus the digit exceeds the line box (sm: 19.1 x 15.4 px), the minimum rule still holds.

Inside Button: the integration writes <Counter size={buttonSize} value={n} /> in the trailing snippet; the counter is centered in the surface (<= 0.5 px) and inherits the content color in every intent, appearance and state; Button fades the trailing slot while loading and hides it from assistive technology; nothing to do in Counter.
